name: Co-location / behind-the-meter
desc: Rules for load sited with generation behind the meter or on the same site, including whether and how it interconnects.

letters.desc: Advanced Energy United supports co-location and hybrid arrangements where load and supply resources are electrically proximate, but insists each configuration be studied and billed based on its actual grid impact rather than under a one-size-fits-all rule.
quotes: United agrees with what appears to be the underlying goal of these principles, which is that large loads should pay for all the services they utilize, and avoid paying for those they do not. However, United cautions that a one-size-fits-all approach is likely insufficient given the variety of possible hybrid or co-located load configurations and the range of different grid services they rely upon.

letters.desc: Amazon Energy supports co-location of large loads at generating facilities and coordinated load and generation interconnection to the bulk electric system. It urges the Commission to expeditiously issue guidance in Docket No. AD24-11-000 on the viability of co-location.
quotes: Amazon Energy supports co-location of large load projects.

Amazon Energy also recognizes there may be benefits for all ratepayers to interconnecting large loads directly to the bulk electric system in coordination with the interconnection of generation facilities.

creating viable pathways to allow large load customers and generators to interconnect to the bulk electric system, and to study, model, and operate with some form of interrelationship would yield benefits for the bulk electric system as a whole, including reduced administration for utilities, RTOs/ISOs, and investors.
Amazon Energy supports solutions that provide the most flexibility to meet the needs of customers and businesses, which can include co-location.

Amazon Energy respectfully encourages the Commission to expeditiously issue an order in the pending proceeding in Docket No. AD24-11-000, which would provide the industry with much needed guidance as to the viability of large loads co-locating at generating facilities going forward.

letters.desc: Siting large loads near existing coal and other generating facilities enables optimized placement, minimizes network upgrade costs, and enhances grid utilization.
quotes: siting new load near or at the same point of interconnection as existing generation such as a coal-fired plant can provide similar efficiencies. Therefore, the Commission should encourage interconnection studies that examine load and hybrid facilities under scenarios that consider location near existing generation to enable optimized siting, minimize network upgrade costs and delays, and enhance grid utilization.

letters.desc: ACC supports explicit recognition of generation and storage co-located at multiple proximities (behind meter, near meter, adjacent to meter) to maximize developer options for grid relief.
quotes: Recognize the value of co-locating generation or storage both behind the meter and near or adjacent to the meter, to ensure no potential solutions are excluded.

letters.desc: AEP endorses the ANOPR's third reform principle that load and generation interconnections should be studied jointly. It argues that proactive planning that integrates both is necessary to avoid the delays produced by treating each as a separate one-off study.
quotes: Consistent with the ANOPR's third Principle for Reform—which encourages studying the interconnection of load and generation together—such proactive planning will necessarily integrate the consideration of both.

letters.desc: Antora notes that the permanent non-firm service it seeks parallels the interim and permanent products from the PJM Co-Location Order, but insists the service must be available to any customer able to meet withdrawal limits, whether or not it is co-located with generation.
quotes: CHILLS' temporary structure mirrors the Interim NITS product that the Commission required PJM to establish in its recent Co-Location Order, but does not fill the additional need the Commission identified in that proceeding, for the transmission provider to offer a permanent non-firm transmission service option.
this service should be available to any customer capable of meeting the necessary withdrawal limitations, whether or not co-located.

letters.desc: Bloom argues that properly structured co-location rules incentivize data centers to bring their own generation, easing resource adequacy strain and shielding existing customers from costs.
quotes: Properly structured hybrid facility interconnection procedures will incentivize data centers to deploy on-site generation that meets their peak loads, thereby easing resource adequacy concerns while protecting existing customers from costs.

letters.desc: CAISO supports policies that accommodate co-located generation and load, including net-rights studies for hybrids and ancillary service provisions, while calling for clear guidance on cost allocation when generation and load upgrade needs are intertwined.
quotes: Hybrid facilities that have strict, unwavering protections like circuit breakers at their point of interconnection should be allowed to have network upgrades based on their net rights requested.  This will save ratepayers and developers from unnecessary costs and help to avoid long construction timelines.

the CAISO requests that any final rule provide clear guidance on cost responsibility for hybrid facilities: Separating which network upgrades were required by a generator and which network upgrades were required by a co-located large load is impractical, if at all possible for some types of upgrades.

letters.desc: The Center supports co-locating data centers with solar and wind to expand capacity without fossil fuel strain, but opposes co-location arrangements that let data centers avoid paying delivery charges and shift costs to other ratepayers.
quotes: Co-locating data centers with solar and/or wind would protect and promote grid reliability by expanding data center capacity while avoiding further strain on the grid.

utilities are getting away with socializing the costs of the data center boom, and simultaneously keeping rates low to attract data centers, by: (1) entering into special contracts; (2) taking advantage of discrepancies between federal and state regulations over cost allocation; and (3) relying on co-location agreements.

letters.org: CHAMBER OF COMMERCE OF THE UNITED STATES
letters.desc: The Chamber urges the Commission to promptly finalize its pending colocation proceeding so that generation-with-load policy is aligned and mutually reinforcing with this rulemaking.
quotes: the Commission should promptly finalize its pending proceeding regarding the colocation of generation with such large loads. A holistic approach is necessary

letters.desc: Chevron, as a natural gas generation developer targeting data center co-location, strongly backs FERC action to expedite hybrid co-location interconnections. It wants the rulemaking to maximize new generation buildout tied to data centers and calls on FERC to create a separate, expedited co-located load and generation interconnection process.
quotes: Chevron encourages the Commission to seize this opportunity to facilitate the expedited interconnection of large loads and generation to support it, including co-located generation.

The Commission should ensure that the steps it takes in this proceeding prioritize the development of hybrid arrangements that involve major investments in new generation resources to achieve the maximum electric supply buildout necessary for domestic data centers as soon as practicable.

letters.desc: CEBA urges FERC to formally recognize co-location of large loads with generation or storage as an authorized, high-value configuration. Co-location reduces congestion, line losses, and transmission upgrade costs. FERC should also complete its PJM co-location review and extend resulting tariff clarity to all markets.
quotes: Hybrid projects can utilize generation and storage technologies that have a strong operational track record in terms of responding to balancing authority dispatch requirements.

The Commission should explicitly recognize that co-locating large loads with generation, whether existing or new, provides meaningful system benefits and should be treated as an authorized interconnection configuration and be studied in a way that reflects their reduced system impact.
FERC should complete its review expeditiously and determine if PJM's tariff, as well as those of other electricity markets, need clearer rules to ensure grid reliability and fair allocation of costs.

letters.desc: ClearPath calls on FERC to ensure that dispatchable large loads and their co-located generating facilities are fully compensated for energy and ancillary services provided to the grid.
quotes: FERC must ensure that dispatchable large loads, in addition to co-located generating facilities, are fully compensated for providing energy and ancillary services to the grid.

letters.desc: AI-SCA endorses co-location and hybrid facilities as pathways that can speed up grid connection for data centers while keeping cost responsibility with the interconnecting customer.
quotes: Approaches such as direct market access and new supply arrangements, such as co-location (or hybrid facilities), bring your own power, and behind-the-meter generation, can enable faster connection to the grid for large load customers like data centers, reshoring of manufacturing, and other industrial processes while ensuring that interconnecting customers are responsible for associated costs of network upgrades.

letters.desc: Constellation supports co-location rules that treat existing and new generation equally. It opposes BYOG proposals that extend expedited treatment only to new generators and argues such proposals would suppress merchant capacity and push existing resources into premature retirement.
quotes: the Commission should affirm its jurisdiction over large load interconnections to the transmission system generally and to hybrid facilities (i.e., the generator and load sharing an interconnection to the interstate grid) in particular.
The Commission should reject undue discrimination against existing generation. This includes "Bring Your Own Generation" proposals in which only new generation resources are eligible to participate.

letters.desc: Constellation supports clear rules enabling both behind-the-meter and hybrid in-front-of-the-meter co-location, pointing to unrebutted PJM record evidence of Transmission Owner discrimination against these configurations. The filing rejects BYOG proposals that favor new over existing generation and argues existing generators have the right to serve any willing customer.
quotes: the Commission should (i) act quickly, (ii) focus relief in regions where there is evidence of undue discrimination, undue preference or unjust and unreasonable service, (iii) respect regional differences, and (iv) avoid unnecessary jurisdictional fights.

the Commission should issue an order on the merits in the PJM Show Cause proceedings and thereby: (i) take swift action to kickstart development on several stalled hyperscale data center projects in PJM; (ii) conclude, based on the comprehensive record in those proceedings, that the lack of clear rules allows the PJM Transmission Owners to unduly discriminate by still refusing to process large load behind-the-meter projects

In PJM, the Commission already has a comprehensive record, including substantial, unrebutted evidence of undue discrimination by PJM Transmission Owners against any behind-the-meter configuration, and any in front-of-the-meter configuration that avoids interconnection through the Transmission Owners' distribution facilities.

Some Transmission Owners have blocked behind-the-meter configurations and are extending that discrimination to front-of-the-meter connections to the grid (hybrid facilities), requiring that these facilities take distribution service or adopt configurations that would make net billing impossible.

they are instead leveraging their monopoly over interconnection to block innovative and efficient configurations that would provide customers with alternatives to the other services (e.g., gross-billed network transmission service and distribution service) these Transmission Owners provide.

the Commission has jurisdiction over hybrid facilities' shared point of interconnection. This is an easy call since the Commission already exercises jurisdiction over the generator's interconnection, and jurisdiction over the same shared facilities does not bifurcate between state and federal authority depending on the services of the moment.

the Commission should reject "Bring Your Own Generation" or "BYOG" proposals (such as PJM Option 6 in the Show Cause proceeding) that would allow state-favored resources to leapfrog the PJM queue, and should likewise reject proposals discussed in the ANOPR comments or in the IMM's recent complaint that would condition new large load interconnections (or expedited interconnection) upon the load bringing its own new generation.

Discrimination against existing generation resources will undermine resource adequacy by signaling that existing capacity is less valuable than new capacity in serving load, even when existing capacity can serve load more efficiently.

Rolling billions of dollars of network upgrades into rate base is not an intuitive way of "protecting customers." Regardless, the Commission's policy should create strong incentives for co-location because co-location minimizes upgrade costs, and that is ultimately what protects consumers.

No Transmission Owner can expedite service or study processing for projects taking the Transmission Owner's preferred type of service or configuration, or refuse to process a complete large load interconnection request on the ground that the large load has not 'arranged for wholesale transmission or retail distribution service.'

letters.desc: Constellation supports co-location of generation and load as an ANOPR principle and proposes LCEP as the specific mechanism. Siting new generation and load at an existing plant's POI reduces network upgrade needs and speeds interconnection.
quotes: Constellation submits these supplemental comments to outline a new, reliable, speed-to-service option pairing new generation with large loads at existing power plant sites of at least the same size, and to urge this option's inclusion in the Commission's next steps on the Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking.

This proposal achieves Secretary Wright's objective "to ensure efficient, timely, and non-discriminatory [large] load interconnections" by adding paired new generation and load without changing injection rights or creating withdrawal rights at existing generation sites.

LCEP Service also is fully responsive to the ANOPR's directives and principles, including to study load together with Generating Facilities, given "siting a large load near or at the same point of interconnection as a new generating facility could reduce the network upgrades needed to interconnect only the load or only the generating facility" (Third Principle), and incentivizing co-location which can "ensure[] efficient buildout of the transmission system" (Fifth Principle).

letters.desc: Critical Loop asks FERC to treat co-located or adjacent resources behind the same point of interconnection as creditable under the LLFC, with joint study of load and supply. The framework should be resource-agnostic so long as a certified power-control system enforces import limits and non-export at the POI.
quotes: Create a non‑firm network service (withdrawal) option and allow non‑firm injection for hybrid or adjacent resources participating in LLFCs, with joint study for load and supply at or near a common point of interconnection

letters.desc: Critical Loop supports recognizing co-located generation and storage as part of the LLFC solution. The filing asks that co-located resources be explicitly modeled in studies rather than treated as absent, and that bring-your-own-capacity arrangements address the generation bottleneck alongside the transmission bottleneck.
quotes: Critical Loop proposed a Large-Load Flexibility Commitment ("LLFC") construct that would allow large loads to interconnect faster when they commit to enforceable operating envelopes supported by on-site or adjacent resources, backed by telemetry, verification, and non-performance provisions.

An LLFC-style flexible connection can address the transmission bottleneck by defining a mix of firm and conditional service within an operating envelope, while complementary "bring your own capacity" mechanisms can address the generation bottleneck by ensuring that the firm portion of the load is backed by accredited capacity paid for by the customer.

we ask the Commission to ensure that flexible solutions and LLFCs are studied on a basis that can be compared with traditional upgrades. This occurs by requiring transmission providers to explicitly model enforceable flexibility and operating envelopes, rather than defaulting to static maximum-withdrawal assumptions that treat all co-located resources as absent or charging.

letters.desc: Crusoe argues that co-locating generation with load materially reduces transmission grid impact and should be recognized in both the study process and the allocation of interconnection costs.
quotes: hybrid facilities combining interconnection requests with onsite generation should be prioritized as they can reduce load requirements while potentially supporting the grid during peak demand.

Joint interconnection studies for hybrid facilities that bring new generation with load will expedite the interconnection process and minimize the need for costly and time-consuming construction of network upgrades because the impact of the new load can be offset by the addition of new generation.

Hybrid facility structures cause significantly less impact on the transmission grid than large loads that do not bring generation.  Thus, where hybrid facilities are proposed, the load and generation should be studied together to get an accurate picture of the load's impact on the grid.

letters.desc: DEC recommends a single unified interconnection study process for projects that combine generation and load at the same point of interconnection, replacing the current system that forces separate studies and produces conflicting assumptions.
quotes: The Commission should require transmission providers to establish a single, integrated interconnection process under their OATTs for projects that combine generation and load at the same point of interconnection.

Current procedures force developers to complete separate studies for generation and load, even when they are part of a single co-located facility. This duplication increases costs, creates conflicting assumptions, and slows project development.

letters.desc: DPN favors studying hybrids by the injection and withdrawal rights requested because it incentivizes co-location with new generation and efficient transmission buildout.
quotes: This provides incentives for co-location with new generation facilities and ensures efficient buildout of the transmission system.

letters.desc: EDF asks the Commission to avoid one-size-fits-all rules that would penalize innovative co-location models. The framework should recognize the range of hybrid structures, from fully behind-the-meter load to network-connected load requiring firm service.
quotes: the Commission should adopt a flexible, performance-based framework that (1) recognizes the diversity within the large load industries (e.g., AI, crypto mining, hydrogen, e-fuels, and carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS)); (2) encourages "grid-light" development structures, such as hybrid facilities that put minimal stress on the grid, and avoids inadvertently penalizing innovative co-located load configuration models; and (3) addresses much needed reforms to the Commission's Public Utility Holding Company Act (PUHCA) regulations to allow independent power producers, such as exempt wholesale generators (EWGs), to make direct sales to large loads (in states where it is allowed) without losing PUHCA exemptions for upstream owners.
Loads with considerable operating flexibility, such as crypto mining load, should not be treated the same as AI data centers that need "five-nines" power reliability.

letters.desc: EEI supports gross-load cost allocation for co-located facilities to prevent large loads from disguising their transmission dependence through netting arrangements that would shift costs to other customers.
quotes: to ensure fairness and avoid implementation complexity, the Commission should make a gross load approach the default for both ancillary services and transmission, subject to exception only if a utility supports and the state approves a different approach.
The Commission should not adopt a default rule that could disguise some large load customers' level of reliance on the transmission system.

letters.desc: EEI cites the FERC order directing PJM to establish transparent rules for AI data centers co-located with generating facilities as part of the forward progress that federal policy should build on rather than displace.
quotes: Commission orders across several regions that: Direct PJM to establish transparent rules to facilitate service of AI-driven data centers and other large loads co-located with generating facilities.

letters.desc: EPSA urges FERC to act first on co-located large load arrangements by drawing on the extensive PJM show cause record. This guidance can and should proceed separately from the broader rulemaking and must not disrupt ongoing commercial transactions.
quotes: EPSA urges the Commission to move forward with direction and guidance for co-located arrangements based on the extensive record set out in the PJM Show Cause proceeding on these issues.

issuing guidance for co-located load arrangements should be task one in the near term for the Commission. This action does not need to run concurrently with any next steps in this rulemaking proceeding

EPSA continues to urge the Commission to ensure that consideration and development of the next step in the instant rulemaking proceeding does not delay, hamper, or interfere with ongoing commercial transactions and arrangements.

letters.desc: ELCON has advocated for co-location flexibility in prior proceedings and extends that position here, urging that hybrid load-plus-generation configurations be accommodated in interconnection studies.
quotes: Varying configurations of large loads, sometimes combined with behind-the-meter generation, must be considered in interconnection studies to allow for the most efficient solutions to serving large loads.

letters.desc: ECA identifies the absence of clear pathways to align load interconnection with the generation and storage resources that large customers build or contract as a core problem requiring FERC action.
quotes: Commission action on large load interconnection to the transmission system is needed to ensure just and reasonable rates and prevent undue discrimination and will open new opportunities to meet the needs of new large loads for "speed to power" while protecting other customers from harm.

Large load customers like data centers, manufacturers, and industry are seeking opportunities to pay for and accelerate timelines for the generation and transmission infrastructure needed to serve them, but are stymied by inconsistent and unclear rules for large load interconnection to transmission, a lack of clear paths to line up load interconnection with the interconnection and delivery of generation they construct or contract to serve them, and fractured and incomplete transmission planning processes that fail to holistically account for projected new large loads and associated generation

letters.desc: Enchanted Rock advocates for adoption of the LCDG framework, whereby load and generation are separately metered but studied together for interconnection and planning. LCDG provides interim power via on-site generation while transmission upgrades are built, mitigating transmission constraints.
quotes: LCDG is a practical and effective solution that would mitigate transmission constraints and address growing electricity demand associated with the influx of large load facilities.

LCDG would mitigate the risk of stranded infrastructure costs falling upon existing grid customers because it would ensure that new large loads would be investing in needed generation resources as they interconnect to the transmission system.

Under circumstances where transmission is unavailable, under LCDG, on-site generation assets would serve as prime power to the large load facility that are waiting for transmission upgrades to be built.

letters.desc: The filer promotes co-locating generation with load so planners study the assets as a combined facility, which it says speeds power delivery, expedites study timelines, triggers fewer upgrades, and reduces strain on transmission infrastructure.
quotes: Enchanted Rock encourages the Commission to adopt rules that will facilitate joint study processes (even if only for a provisional period) and that evaluate co-located and hybrid facilities based on their net impacts to the grid.

This observation highlights the value of co-location and its practical application to facilitate speed-to-power, expedite study timelines, protect ratepayer affordability, and reduce strain on transmission infrastructure.
Co-locating generation with load allows system planners to

letters.desc: ENGIE views co-location of generation and storage with large loads as the primary solution to grid impact. Net metering of co-located resources reduces upgrade needs, ratepayer costs, and ancillary service overcharges. Charging on gross peak demand without netting penalizes facilities that have already reduced their grid footprint.
quotes: Co-locating large loads with generation and/or storage should be emphasized as the primary solution to impacts caused by large loads interconnecting to the bulk electric system.

Allowing large loads and co-located generation to net meter is the most efficient way to interconnect large loads. Netting of load and generation reduces the need for unnecessary system upgrades and associated costs, and decreases the need for subsidies which reduces ratepayer costs.

ENGIE finds this principle is problematic because it ignores the operational reality and fairness considerations of hybrid facilities. If facilities are charged based solely on peak demand, without netting co-located generation, it treats the site as if the generation does not exist.

letters.org: Entergy Services, LLCEntergy New Orleans, LLCEntergy Louisiana, LLC ,Entergy Mississippi, LLC ,Entergy Arkansas, LLC ,Entergy Texas, Inc. ,
letters.desc: Entergy argues that its state retail regulatory frameworks already include efficient rules for attracting and interconnecting large loads, and asks that any federal action avoid displacing that collaborative state process.
quotes: the existing retail regulatory frameworks in the Entergy Operating Companies' service territories include efficient rules for attracting and interconnecting large loads, and which provide for significant input from retail regulators.

If the Commission nonetheless does take any action, it should recognize that the Entergy Operating Companies' respective public service commissions provided the collaboration, oversight, and direction needed to achieve the successes discussed above.  It should take care to avoid any rule that could interfere with successful existing state processes.

letters.desc: Eolian supports allowing hybrid resources that are not strictly co-located but are electrically proximate to be studied together, and urges FERC to define hybrid facilities broadly enough to include storage and configurations across different ownership and meter arrangements.
quotes: the Commission should direct transmission providers to offer non-firm or conditional firm transmission service to hybrid resources that allow them to inject and withdraw up to their full potential, subject to specified system conditions and their flexibility commitments.

letters.desc: Eolian supports a configuration-neutral co-location standard based on de-minimis loop flows (no more than 3% through ties to the network and 1% over other transmission facilities) rather than a same-point-of-interconnection requirement, which it argues would exclude projects with no reliability justification.
quotes: Consistent with ANOPR Principles Three, Five, and Six, integrated joint study of hybrid load and generation facilities based on requested withdrawal and injection rights is critical to enabling rapid, affordable interconnection of large loads and hybrids.

We urge the Commission to set standards that allow for configurations to flexibly navigate commercial and local regulatory considerations while adhering to demonstrable de-minimis impacts on the transmission system and thereby qualifying for expedited interconnection.

letters.desc: Eolian supports extending co-location-style benefits to loads served by adjacent (electrically proximate) generation, not only loads at the same point of interconnection. It argues that PJM's Co-Location Order is a useful starting point but must be broadened to cover adjacent arrangements.
quotes: we have not encountered any transmission provider that currently has a process which (i) adequately integrates or coordinates the interconnection of supply resources and load, (ii) provides developers of supply resources such as Eolian with adequate incentive to locate generation and storage assets in a manner that opens additional system headroom for load interconnection, or (iii) offers the full range of transmission service options necessary to allow supply and load to coordinate to optimally use the existing system and reduce transmission infrastructure needs.

The Commission must require transmission providers to offer transmission services that match the ability of loads to use the capabilities of adjacent generation, including non-firm and reduced service options. Such service must allow the load to take service when the grid is unconstrained and the supply resource is not available (including when a battery resource is charging) while electing to curtail when the grid is constrained.

the Commission should explicitly direct transmission providers to make the non-firm services available to all loads willing and able to limit withdrawals from the transmission system rather than limiting availability only to co-located loads.

the generation interconnection process afforded generators the ability to generate 'tags' representing the transmission capacity that the proposed generation opens. Such a transmission capacity tag could then be used in the load interconnection process, allowing load to contract with generation to support development that enables development to move forward that is currently on hold.

letters.desc: esVolta urges FERC to clarify that front-of-the-meter BESS configurations count as hybrid facilities under any large-load rulemaking, and that both on-site co-location and nearby standalone configurations are eligible supply arrangements for serving large loads.
quotes: Given its fast deployment, data centers would benefit from the ability to share interconnection rights with existing storage interconnection rights.

the Commission should clarify that consistent with the Commission's Large Generator Interconnection Procedures, it intends for energy storage to be accommodated and included in its definition of "hybrid facilities" within the context of any proceeding aimed at ensuring the timely and orderly interconnection of large loads.

the Commission should also expand its view of the load-supply configurations and expressly state that front-of-the-meter BESS configurations are also eligible configurations to serve large loads as many data centers are actively pursuing such arrangements.

esVolta encourages the Commission to consider a similar approach in any rulemaking it promulgates to address the integration of large loads and ensure that standalone BESS either located "in close proximity", "near by" the data center, or either electrically or co-located onsite with the data center or the large load is deemed an eligible supply resource to receive expedited interconnection study treatment along with the data center load.

letters.desc: ETX argues that both front-of-meter and behind-the-meter co-location arrangements should be recognized in the study framework. Studying only net injection/withdrawal would effectively exclude FTM co-location, even though such arrangements can provide equal or greater reliability benefits.
quotes: The Load Interconnection Study Procedures should allow for flexible project sizing amendments based on study results that encourage efficient use of transmission resources, especially for Hybrid and/or co-located projects where parallel load and generation studies will create modeling circularities.

Co-located facilities should not be studied based on the "net" amount of injection/withdrawal rights requested – to do so implies the Docket is applicable only to "behind the meter" ("BTM") co-located facilities, and misrepresents the broader potential benefits of co-location.

A load with a "front of the meter" ("FTM"), market-facing interconnection co-located with generation with a FTM interconnection, even if commercially distinct and not electrically "netting" injection/withdrawal, may have equal or greater benefits to grid reliability (total network upgrades, resource adequacy, transmission constraints, etc.) than co-located BTM facilities.
If a project cannot achieve that through lower network upgrade costs, it should not be incentivized to do so with an off-set crediting mechanism.

letters.desc: Eversource asks the final rule to accommodate loads co-located with generation and to let transmission providers set region-specific rules governing co-located generator interconnection rights.
quotes: the final rule should also be flexible enough to encompass different “hybrid” load arrangements, including those co-located with generation seeking standby service, behind-the-meter generation with voluntary curtailment/isolation, and other arrangements that may be sought by customers.

The final rule should also be flexible enough to allow transmission providers to develop and address region-specific rules and concerns (such as termination of co-located generator interconnection rights).

letters.desc: Fervo emphasizes that co-locating firm, dispatchable generation with load substantially reduces transmission reinforcement needs and that transition rules and cost allocation should recognize these system benefits.
quotes: Hybrid geothermal facilities that "bring their own power" can substantially decrease the need for upstream transmission reinforcements by co-locating firm, dispatchable generation with load, often avoiding or minimizing upgrades that a stand-alone load would otherwise require.

Fervo supports the Commission's effort to establish a clear and orderly transition plan and encourages the Commission to design that transition to recognize the system benefits of projects that co-locate large loads with clean generation.

letters.desc: Fluence supports treating energy storage co-located or electrically adjacent to large loads as qualifying for hybrid facility treatment under the interconnection rules.
quotes: the definition of 'hybrid facility' for large loads should also explicitly include energy storage systems.

letters.desc: Geronimo Power argues that net-impact billing creates an incentive for large loads to pursue co-location, which minimizes reliance on the grid and protects captive ratepayers. The ANOPR's ancillary service principle should be revised to credit co-located generation.
quotes: Assessing large loads based on their net impact is not only required by the cost causation principle, it will also accelerate the ability of large loads to obtain power on a timely basis.

principle twelve of the ANOPR states that 'utilities serving large loads, including those at hybrid facilities, should be responsible for ancillary services based on peak demand, without consideration of any co-located generation.'

A better approach for the Commission to take is to treat ancillary service costs in the same manner as it has proposed to treat transmission service charges: large loads pay for ancillary services based on their actual use of, and reliance on, the service at issue.

letters.desc: Google supports co-location and electrically proximate arrangements as incentivized pathways to faster interconnection, but opposes any rule that would make co-location or curtailability a requirement, citing non-discrimination obligations under the Federal Power Act.
quotes: As with the rules governing colocation or electrically proximate pairs of load and generation, and as in SPP's HILL/HILLGA proposal, any new rules governing the interconnection of curtailable load must take the form of an incentive, not a requirement.

letters.desc: Google supports an expedited, coordinated study process for loads and generation behind the same point of interconnection. Co-location minimizes dependence on constrained transmission corridors and raises fewer jurisdictional questions than standalone load interconnection.
quotes: The concerns raised in the record about co-location are readily resolvable, and do not outweigh its potential value in interconnecting new large loads in a manner that maximizes the use of existing infrastructure and minimizes strain on the grid.

Determining what network upgrades are required to accommodate the actual injection and withdrawal rights requested and providing transmission service based on the actual use of the transmission system will send the proper signals to encourage developers to pursue the most efficient projects.

letters.org: Governor Josh Shapiro and Governor Glenn Youngkin
letters.desc: The governors back the proposal's incentives for LLAs to invest in nearby new generation and storage resources and to curtail during tight market conditions.
quotes: this framework would provide strong incentives for LLAs to invest in nearby new energy generation and storage resources, to curtail during tight market conditions, and to take responsibility for their network upgrade costs.

letters.desc: GridCARE urges FERC to study load and any co-located or behind-the-meter resources together, reflecting actual operating conditions. The company specifically argues that non-exporting behind-the-meter storage should be studied as a load-modifying resource rather than as a generator seeking firm deliverability.
quotes: The Commission should also support study approaches that clearly distinguish between non-exporting, load-modifying behind-the-meter resources and true generation resources seeking firm transmission rights.
Applying generator-level deliverability assumptions to non-export configurations can overstate impacts, increase upgrade requirements, and erode the very flexibility the ANOPR seeks to unlock.

letters.desc: GridStor frames ESR charging paired with large load like a co-located behind-the-meter configuration and asks the Commission to recognize this pairing when distinguishing ESR treatment and coordinating studies.
quotes: GridStor submits these comments to assist the Commission as it moves forward with a rulemaking on these issues, emphasizing the need to distinguish the treatment of Energy Storage Resource (“ESR”) charging in the development of a Final Rule or other action that affects the interconnection of large loads.
In particular, we ask that any Commission consideration of such coordinated study include the load side of paired facilities like ESRs, not only the generation side.
The Commission should enable studies of large loads and paired ESRs as coordinated loads, i.e., with integrated control that act as a single resource.

letters.desc: Helion supports streamlining interconnection for generation collocated directly with large loads to reduce transmission congestion while enhancing reliability. The filing proposes simplified procedures and expedited approval for collocated and behind-the-meter generation, noting that collocation eliminates line losses, reduces bulk transmission stress, and allows precise matching of power supply to demand.
quotes: There is a fundamental shift in how America must approach grid planning: the rise of large, concentrated loads requiring direct coordination with generation resources. This insight points toward a solution that reduces transmission congestion while enhancing reliability—collocating generation directly at load centers.

Calling data centers "flexible" does not mean they can simply absorb sudden cuts in power; real flexibility comes from collocated generation that can ramp up and down with their needs and support the grid in the process.

When baseload, dispatchable, non-fuel-limited generation is collocated with large loads, both the interconnection challenge and the generation/transmission capacity challenge can be addressed simultaneously.
Establish simplified procedures for projects pairing large loads with collocated baseload, dispatchable generation that addresses reliability issues
Create expedited approval pathways for behind-the-meter or directly connected generation that reduces demand on shared grid infrastructure

letters.desc: The filer frames co-location as a rational make-vs-buy response to high transaction costs in legacy interconnection rules. She supports extending generator-style interconnection regimes to loads rather than penalizing co-location arrangements.
quotes: Co-location and hybrid configurations are rational economic responses to these high transaction costs ("make vs. buy" decisions) and should be facilitated rather than penalized by extending generator-style interconnection regimes to loads.

letters.desc: Kiesling frames co-location and hybrid configurations as rational institutional responses to high transaction costs and the pacing mismatch, not as bypass strategies to penalize. She argues that extending generator-style rules to loads without modification would worsen rather than resolve these frictions.
quotes: Because large loads are highly elastic and can relocate or self-supply, assigning them full upgrade costs encourages inefficient grid defection.
The hybrid or co-location contracts that large loads and generators are entering are system-enhancing examples of the 'make or buy' decision in institutional economics.
Co-location is a market response to the pacing mismatch between data center speed-to-power and infrastructure construction timeframes.

letters.desc: The filer supports VPPs receiving capacity market compensation for their genuine resource adequacy value, but opposes extending that role into interconnection engineering where different physical standards apply.
quotes: VPPs should continue to receive appropriate compensation through capacity markets for their genuine Resource Adequacy contributions. Data centers should continue to fund interconnection upgrades necessary to maintain physical system reliability.

letters.desc: The filing supports establishing environmental and infrastructure control standards for co-located data centers, including technology deployment, public ownership of infrastructure, and open-source utility interfaces.
quotes: By replacing evaporative water consumption with closed supercritical CO2 cooling loops, implementing phase-change cryogenic freeze-crystallization for agricultural water purification, utilizing medium-voltage solid-state transformers for peak-shaving grid buffering, and implementing dynamic phase-inversion networks for biological EMF cancellation, this framework establishes a baseline for non-poisonous, high-density infrastructure computing.

Any federal, state, or municipal agency granting an interconnection or land-use permit for a data infrastructure asset exceeding 20 Megawatts must condition that approval upon the deployment of an Open-Source Utility Interface.

The public utility and local regulatory authority shall retain exclusive, sovereign ownership over the physical Solid-State Transformer (SST) boundaries and the public, immutable environmental telemetry arrays (The Aegis Protocol).

letters.desc: The filer recommends a federal planning framework for SMR co-location with data centers as the long-range resolution to the firm baseload power problem. SMRs targeting 50 to 300 megawatts are compatible with brownfield industrial parcels and match the scale and timeline of serious data center operators. Rust Belt sites and a closed-loop model for the Southwest are the two proposed deployment paths.
quotes: Small modular reactor technology, with units targeting fifty to three hundred megawatts of output, factory-fabricated modular components, passive safety systems, and siting footprints compatible with brownfield industrial parcels, is the most technically coherent long-range resolution to the firm power problem.

letters.desc: ITI supports comprehensive modeling of generation colocation arrangements and other configurations in interconnection studies, emphasizing that colocation should not be limited to specific arrangements but should include all configurations that reduce upgrade costs.
quotes: ITI supports the principle that load and generation should be studied together. We would like to clarify that this should not be limited to colocation arrangements. If new generating facilities are located at or near new load facilities, then they would both require less transmission and distribution upgrades than if they were studied separately.

Interconnection studies should comprehensively model large load customers' generation colocation arrangements, curtailment abilities, or arrangements with other parties that would result in fewer upgrades. Fewer system upgrades resulting from interconnection studies lead to faster energization timelines for large loads requesting interconnection.

letters.desc: iMasons endorses bring-your-own-generation frameworks on a voluntary basis, noting that co-located generation enhances reliability and reduces upgrade needs. However, these frameworks should not disrupt existing generator interconnection queues.
quotes: iMasons supports studying hybrid facilities together with generating facilities to the greatest extent practical, and studying hybrid facilities based on their requested amount of injection and/or withdrawal rights.

Encouraging hybrid facilities will help solve 'speed to power' issues for data centers, enhance reliability by encouraging data centers to bring their own generation when they interconnect and can alleviate the need for building excess network upgrades, which will benefit consumers.

letters.desc: IFP supports co-location of loads with generation as a key tool for reducing costly network upgrades. Studying hybrid facilities on net injection or withdrawal rights can dramatically shrink grid impact and cut years of interconnection delays.
quotes: Principle 3 encourages the co-location of new loads and generation, which can minimize the need for costly network upgrades.

a 900 MW data center co-located with a 1000 MW generator could request only 100 MW of net injection rights, dramatically reducing its grid impact and avoiding years of delays associated with upgrades.

letters.desc: IECA supports co-location of Data Centers with generation as the preferred pathway, favoring joint federal-state study processes modeled on the DCC BYOG Pathway for regions experiencing delays.
quotes: We submit that a collaborative approach between States and the Commission can produce a process that can simultaneously study both a Data Center and a contractually-associated electric generation resource by joining both (i) the Federal approval of interconnection of the generation resource (through the Commission-regulated LGIP and LGIA process) and (ii) the State approval (through a State-regulated utility) of the interconnection of a new large load.

We fully support the proposal in the ANOPR of simultaneously studying the impacts on the network of one or more large loads (i.e., Data Centers) and one or more associated electric generating facilities as offsetting loads and resources and therefore worthy of expedited consideration and approval as a reasonable approach to addressing the interconnection of Data Centers that co-locate with existing or new electric generation facilities.

letters.desc: IECA supports FERC issuing guidance on acceptable co-location configurations and asks the Commission to define co-location broadly enough to cover loads and generators at proximate (not just identical) points of interconnection. It also urges FERC to draw on the EL25-49 show-cause record when formulating that guidance.
quotes: a large load which interconnects with the grid at one point of interconnection and is contractually tied to one or more comparably-sized generation resources which interconnect with the same grid at a physically "proximate" location, should be viewed as no less physically co-located than a large load and a comparably-sized generation resource that interconnect with the same grid at a single point of interconnection, whether in front of or behind the meter.

We support the simultaneous study of system impacts from a Co-Located Load with its Co-Located Generation and the expeditious approval of the interconnection of both at a single point of interconnection or at two or more "proximate" points of interconnection, provided that the impacts on the transmission grid and other users of that transmission grid are addressed as set forth in Section III.B. of these Reply Comments.

the Commission and its Staff should now have a relatively complete record on "co-location" issues in PJM on which to formulate and propose guidance in response to the ANOPR regarding the range of acceptable transmission system protection provisions that counterparties could apply to co-location arrangements involving large loads and co-located generation resources located at the same point of interconnection or at "proximate" points of interconnection with the interstate transmission grid.

letters.org: Invenergy Wind Development North America LLCInvenergy Solar Development North America LLCInvenergy Thermal Development Holdings LLC ,
letters.desc: Invenergy asks FERC to study hybrid (co-located load and generation) projects as a single entity rather than splitting them into separate load and generation assessments. One combined deposit and one cost-allocation study avoids double-counting security and correctly reflects the net grid impact. HVDC converter stations should qualify for the same expedited co-located treatment as generation.
quotes: transmission owners too often require developers to post billions of dollars in security up front to interconnect hybrid facilities without any regard to the actual cost of interconnecting and serving data center load, in some instances requiring hybrid projects to securitize both the load and generation interconnection requests.

The Commission should also clarify that high voltage, direct current ("HVDC") solutions should be treated as equivalent to co-located generation in the integrated study process, including any expedited study process for co-located (or hybrid) projects.

study deposits for large load and hybrid facilities should be based on the size of the request. For hybrid interconnection requests, there should be only one study deposit that is based on the greater of the generation size or load size, but not both.
hybrid projects should be studied as one project for purposes of assigning network upgrade costs, rather than studying the load and generation separately.

letters.desc: ISO-NE notes that co-locating load and generation for joint study already exists in New England through the cluster study framework. Studying hybrid facilities by net injection and withdrawal rights supports efficient co-location but does not eliminate the need for full interconnection studies.
quotes: ISO-NE is supportive of this principle, the impacts of which would be reflected in study assumptions.  ISO-NE also notes that this principle would not negate the need for Interconnection Studies.

letters.desc: The Alliance strongly favors co-location of large loads with existing or new renewable generation as the primary tool for reducing new transmission buildout and the resulting harm to conserved lands. It recommends pairing data centers with renewables and battery storage where new generation is required.
quotes: governmental taking of lands, including already conserved lands, for the construction of transmission infrastructure, is the most frequent means of grid expansion, as opposed to co-location or other less impactful but equally effective alternatives.
the Alliance recommends the co-location of large energy users, such as data centers, together with existing energy generation sources to minimize the need for new transmission buildout.
Where new energy generation sources are needed, the Alliance recommends the co-location of large-scale energy uses, such as data centers, with renewable energy and battery energy storage systems.

letters.desc: The filing describes generation requirements and customer-owned supply arrangements among the protective tools members use to serve large loads.
quotes: Requires large load customers to procure or contract for their own generation supply.

letters.desc: Maven Solutions argues that any cost-allocation framework must include community hosting standards, not just ratepayer protection. The filing documents 268 opposition groups across 37 states and argues that assigning transmission costs without addressing environmental impact, water use, workforce participation, and tax-revenue transparency will deepen rather than resolve community opposition.
quotes: Maven Solutions' research documents the national scale of community opposition to data-center development: 268 local groups across 37 states, representing over 360,000 members, coordinated through organizations including the Coalition for Responsible Data Center Development.
A framework that assigns transmission costs while ignoring the communities standing next to the transmission facilities will not resolve that opposition. It will deepen it.

letters.desc: Meta advocates for streamlined procedures for co-located large loads and generation, including elimination of additional regulatory hurdles, fair cost-allocation principles for behind-meter siting, concurrent expedited study processes, and clarity on pre-grid-connection deployment without prior utility approval.
quotes: Meta strongly supports expedited review of facilities that co-locate large loads and generation. Co-location allows large loads to secure electric power quickly, and, in some instances, streamline the build out of necessary transmission infrastructure
Coordination of new load and incremental new generation allows data centers to meet their power demands without resorting to curtailment commitments and therefore warrants expedited study
the Commission should clarify that large load and generation sharing a common point of interconnection do not require additional regulatory hurdles solely due to their co-located configuration

when generation to power large load is sited behind the meter, regulators should use cost-allocation principles that ensure no negative impacts to grid reliability or unfair cost shifts to other customers
the Commission should call on utilities and grid operators to promptly develop streamlined study processes to study large load and incremental generation simultaneously and on an expedited basis

the Commission should clarify the conditions under which co-located load and new generation may be sited and initially operated without utility or grid operator approval, in advance of later connection to the grid pursuant to interconnection procedures

letters.desc: The filer supports MISO's proposed Zero-Injection Generator Interconnection Agreement, which would allow a generator to serve co-located load directly without receiving interconnection service. This approach is designed to reduce network upgrades and is expected to be filed with FERC in June 2026.
quotes: MISO's proposed ZGIA is specifically designed with that goal in mind. The ZGIA would allow a generator to serve load directly but grants no interconnection service.
The proposed ZGIA process leverages existing interconnection frameworks in terms of study aspects, timing, and financial/other obligations.

letters.desc: The Monitor's preferred solution is a requirement that new large data center loads procure new generation with locational and temporal characteristics matched to their load profile. This approach would avoid imposing reliability and cost burdens on other customers, and an expedited queue option could be offered to loads that comply.
quotes: The market solution is to require new large data center loads to bring their own new generation with locational and temporal characteristics matched to their load profile.
If large new data center loads want an expedited interconnection process, loads should be required to bring their own new generation.

letters.desc: National Grid supports exemptions or tailored study tracks for hybrid co-located facilities where on-site generation primarily serves the associated load. This avoids subjecting data center projects to the full 567-day NYISO cluster study cycle and encourages co-location.
quotes: Rather than subjecting these projects to full cluster study timelines, the Commission could explore exemptions or streamlined processes for hybrid facilities where generation is primarily intended to serve the associated load.

letters.desc: Hybrid facilities approval processes should grant states the same discretion they have over new generation resources.
quotes: any approval process for hybrid facilities should allow states the same discretion they currently have over new generation.

letters.org: New York Independent System Operator, Inc.
letters.desc: NYISO endorses requiring reliability studies when a generating facility exits markets to serve co-located load, and asks that such studies cover both transmission security and resource adequacy. It requests flexibility for ISOs to design these studies in a way compatible with existing deactivation study processes.
quotes: The NYISO supports the requirement for ISO/RTOs to establish procedures to study, and ensure, that the exit or suspension of an existing generating facility, in whole or in part, from participation in the wholesale and ancillary markets to serve load does not result in reliability issues on its system.

any proposed rule must allow ISO/RTOs to develop a process to assess the reliability impact of an existing generating facility that seeks to exit or suspend participation in order to serve new load directly.  Such assessment should include both transmission security as well as resource adequacy impacts.

letters.desc: NREMC supports front-of-meter interconnection for hybrid facilities with full transparency on load and generation components. This approach enables transmission providers to accurately study system impacts, appropriately allocate costs, and maintain clear operational visibility.
quotes: All load and generation configurations, including hybrid arrangements, should interconnect on a front-of-the-meter basis, with full transparency regarding both the load and the generating components. Transparent, front-of-the-meter interconnection ensures that transmission providers can accurately study system impacts (including contingency scenarios at the hybrid facilities), appropriately allocate costs, and maintain clear operational visibility.

letters.desc: Ohio FEA strongly supports 'Bring Your Own Generation' concepts with expedited interconnection for generation paired in proximity to new load, provided that any existing generation suspending grid service must study reliability impacts at its own expense.
quotes: the Ohio FEA strongly supports 'Bring Your Own Generation' concepts as a means to bring much needed new generation online to meet the massive demand of new large loads, including expedited interconnection for new generation paired in proximity to new load

any existing generating resource that suspends grid service in order to serve new load must undergo studies at their own expense to ensure those arrangements do not undermine the reliability of the bulk power system

letters.desc: Hybrid facilities placing generation and load at the same point reduce transmission expansion needs. Study methodologies should evaluate co-located systems on net impact (actual rights) rather than gross characteristics, with study assumptions matching actual operational parameters.
quotes: Our model internalizes the costs of powering specific large loads—our business model does not require and does not seek to shift costs to captive ratepayers.
Advanced nuclear technology allows reliable, carbon-free, baseload power to be generated close to large loads, minimizing the need for costly transmission investments.
hybrid facilities should be studied based on the amount of injection and/or withdrawal rights requested. This focus on net impact, rather than gross characteristics, is critical.
Methodologies should not default to 'worst-case' assumptions (e.g., assuming co-located generation is offline during peak load) if the facility is not configured to operate that way.

letters.desc: OpenAI backs co-located load-plus-generation configurations, asking that on-site or behind-the-meter generation be credited through net-impact evaluation.
quotes: OpenAI supports a clear pathway for load paired with on-site or behind-the-meter generationtobeevaluatedonanet-impactbasistocapturerealsystemeffectsandreducestudy burdensandduration.

letters.desc: OpenAI endorses integration of co-located generation and storage with large loads as part of a comprehensive framework to protect the grid and enable faster interconnection.
quotes: A framework that enables Grid Flexibility, integrates co-located generation and storage, aligns cost responsibility with national infrastructure benefits, and enforces consistent timelines will not only protect the grid—it will help unlock the next era of American reindustrialization, technological leadership, and democratic economic growth.

letters.desc: OPSI supports the concept of studying load and co-located generation together as a way to encourage large loads to bring their own generation, potentially easing resource adequacy concerns.
quotes: If large load additions come with its own generation and FERC promotes the more efficient study of generation and load together, this could be an incentive for these loads to bring their own generation.

letters.org: Pennsylvania Office of Consumer AdvocateDelaware Division of the Public Advocate
letters.desc: The filers support co-located and hybrid facilities but condition interconnection approval on the large load bringing sufficient offsetting capacity to avoid worsening resource adequacy in the PJM region.
quotes: The Joint Consumer Advocates support large loads and hybrid facilities that interconnect to the system only if they bring sufficient capacity (either through generation and reserves or capacity-backed demand response) to offset the additional load brought onto the grid.

letters.org: Pennsylvania Office of Consumer AdvocateDelaware Division of the Public AdvocateIllinois Office of Attorney General ,
letters.desc: The filers recommend that hybrid facilities with co-located generation be metered and studied on a gross load basis, not net, to prevent free-riding on the transmission system and subsidization by other customers.
quotes: FERC should approach injection and withdrawal rights according to grid-protective assumptions that prevent free-riding and regulatory evasion.
the Joint Consumer Advocates recommend that hybrid facilities have their load and generation components metered separately, to ensure fair and accurate cost allocation of transmission costs.

letters.desc: PJM argues that many ANOPR co-location principles are already addressed through its necessary study process and existing dockets, suggesting some FERC action may be redundant. It recommends FERC assess resource adequacy impacts of hybrid configurations as part of the just-and-reasonable standard.
quotes: Many of these principles could be addressed through the existing PJM necessary study process that PJM previously utilized to study, develop, and modify existing generator interconnections and agreements seeking to co-locate large loads.  This effectively means no FERC action may be needed to accomplish some of the proposed reforms in certain instances.

FERC could assess whether hybrid configurations are resource adequacy positive (thus closing the supply-demand gap) or, at a minimum, resource adequacy neutral when determining whether such configurations are just and reasonable.

the proposed reforms appear to signal an openness to a less-reliable planning paradigm for new generation facilities (see, e.g., Principles 3 and 5) where hybrid facilities involving "new generation facilities" are studied based solely on injection and/or withdrawal rights requested, and large loads and hybrid facilities that agree to be curtailable will have their studies expedited so that such facilities can be put into operation with greater speed.

letters.desc: PPL supports co-location rules that require separate metering, system protection facilities, and transmission service charges based on the load's full withdrawal rights rather than a netted value. These conditions allow co-location benefits while preventing subsidization of new loads by network customers.
quotes: any Commission action on co-located load should follow two 'North Star' principles: (1) Protect the safety and reliability of the bulk electric system; and (2) Prevent subsidization of new loads by network customers.

hybrid facilities 'shall be required to install the system protection facilities necessary to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals that exceed the respective rights.' Here again, the ANOPR hits the mark exactly.
Transmission service should not be based on a netted value with the generator, as this risks undercharging for use based on the characteristics of the generator and the load.

letters.desc: Islanded CRE systems pose no cascading failure risk to the broader grid because they are not physically connected. Section 215's cascading-failure rationale does not apply to isolated systems, making FERC oversight unnecessary.
quotes: Further, because such systems are not connected to the grid, they cannot cause cascading failures or impact the reliability of the broader network. Section 215 was enacted in response to the 2003 Northeast blackout, which cascaded across multiple states precisely because interconnected facilities affected one another.

letters.org: PSEG CompaniesPSEG Energy Resources & Trade LLCPSEG Power LLC ,Public Service Electric and Gas Company ,
letters.desc: PSEG supports co-location arrangements as an efficient use of the transmission system and urges the Commission not to subject them to discriminatory study requirements or gross-load billing. Co-located loads should be treated the same as existing BTMG customers.
quotes: the Commission should provide data centers with the flexibility and optionality to select a configuration that best fits their particular circumstances and needs, including in front of the meter connections or co-location/behind the meter configurations.

applying such a study to co-located load arrangement would be unduly discriminatory under the FPA because it would treat co-located load arrangements differently than loads seeking to interconnect on a front of the meter basis.
it would be inappropriate to consider resource adequacy issues in the study process for co-located load/hybrid arrangements.

a transmission pricing methodology for a co-located arrangement that is based on gross load without any consideration for actual usage of the transmission system or the impact or use of the transmission system would clearly fail to comply with cost causation principles.
co-located load is using the transmission system in the same manner as BTMG customers and there would be no justification to treat behind the meter load different from BTMG.
network upgrades required by co-location load arrangements should continue to be directly assigned to the co-location arrangements.

letters.desc: RSI proposes that federalized interconnection extend to hybrid load-generation and behind-the-meter configurations that seek wholesale market participation, citing their resource adequacy and network upgrade benefits over demand-only loads.
quotes: FERC should conduct a rulemaking permitting Commission-jurisdictional interconnection processes for load, but only where the interconnection is necessary to offer or receive an otherwise wholesale market service.

accelerating the interconnection of these load-and-FERC-jurisdictional-service configurations is warranted, given their outsized contribution to resource adequacy and limiting the impact on the broader transmission network.
the Commission should use the expertise and evidence it has accumulated in Docket Nos. EL25-49, AD24-11 and EL25-20 to effectuate RSI's proposal.

letters.desc: Studying large loads together with co-located generation helps identify and mitigate network constraints, protecting residential customers from unnecessary upgrade costs.
quotes: Studying large loads together with co-located generation can help identify and mitigate network constraints and protect customers, especially residential customers, from avoidable upgrade costs.

letters.desc: SMA supports co-location of large loads with BESS and generation as a way to reduce costly network upgrades and maintain stability. Facilities that self-supply ancillary services should receive priority connection pathways and compensation.
quotes: Advanced grid-forming inverters with BESS can reduce the need for costly infrastructure expenditures, which would otherwise be borne by consumers.
A key consideration for hybrid facilities serving large, variable loads such as data centers is the highly dynamic load profile, which can pose challenges for maintaining system stability.
SMA supports prioritizing large loads, especially when co-located with generation, provided that power system stability is maintained and further price increases are avoided.

SMA suggests allowing a 'priority setup' to be connected, where facilities with their own infrastructure that already supports grid stability - such as BESS with advanced grid-forming capabilities - can provide all relevant ancillary services and receive appropriate incentives (e.g. compensation fees or easy connection process).

letters.desc: SEIA supports flexible co-location frameworks, including BYOG with VPP aggregations, but draws a line at preferential access. Co-located generators seeking injection rights beyond load service must use the standard queue, and BYOG generators should be in the same electrical zone as the load. SEIA urges the Commission to create incentives for new generation rather than repurposing retiring units.
quotes: The Commission should instead require transmission providers to develop methodologies that allocate ancillary service and transmission costs in proportion to the level of service and reliability actually used by each customer.
The Commission should also make explicit that BYOG arrangements may include Distributed Energy Resource Aggregations (sometimes referred to as 'Virtual Power Plants' (VPPs)).
SEIA urges the Commission to establish incentives and efficient processes to encourage large loads to bring their own, new generation.

letters.desc: SPP's High Impact Large Load process and MISO's Expedited Project Review provide proven, stakeholder-vetted frameworks that expedite large load interconnection while respecting state and federal jurisdictions and protecting incumbent utilities. These should be adopted as the model for any FERC-wide approach.
quotes: SPP has worked to expedite the interconnection of large loads such as with their High Impact Large Load (HILL) proposal, recently filed with FERC. The HILL process provides an excellent framework for an interconnection process that meets the rapidly increasing demand for electricity while leaving state jurisdiction intact, protecting legacy customers, and promoting regulatory certainly.

The SPP and MISO approaches to large load interconnection represent well-vetted processes which resulted from significant stakeholder input and buy-in. Both approaches help to address the challenges associated with large load customers while respecting and maintaining state and federal jurisdiction.

The SDPUC supports the work the RTOs are doing and would advocate for a similar large load interconnection process, one that is limited in scope, to be adopted should FERC move forward with a rule making.

letters.org: Southern Environmental Law CenterAppalachian VoicesNorth Carolina Sustainable Energy Association ,South Carolina Coastal Conservation League ,Southern Alliance for Clean Energy ,
letters.desc: The filers support co-location rules that require accurate identification of costs borne by co-located loads, ensure co-located loads pay applicable transmission service rates, and prevent bilateral contracts with existing generators from raising capacity prices or reducing resource adequacy for other ratepayers.
quotes: If the Commission allows transmission-connected load to co-locate with generation, it must protect existing ratepayers and other interconnection customers from cost, reliability, and competitive impacts.

letters.desc: SMECO supports expanding reliability must-run studies for existing generators entering partial suspension to serve co-located or hybrid large load configurations to ensure local reliability is not compromised.
quotes: SMECO appreciates the importance of ANOPR Principle 10 and urges the Commission to adopt a final rule to ensure that local reliability is not negatively impacted by hybrid/co-location arrangements, if such arrangements are to be permitted in the first instance at all.

SMECO supports a final rule that would consider expanding the reliability studies that PJM performs pursuant to PJM Tariff, Part V to an existing generating facility that seeks to enter a partial suspension, as described in the ANOPR, to serve any new load authorized to take service in a co-located or hybrid configuration.

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: The group supports co-location frameworks that allow grid-connected generation within a defined electrical proximity to serve large loads, provided each is separately metered and transmission charges apply to gross load withdrawals. It also supports requiring an SSR/RMR study before an existing generator partially suspends to serve a co-located load.
quotes: It is essential that any large load rulemaking facilitate the ability to serve new loads with grid-connected generation in a manner similar to the SPP HILL Proposal.
the load also may be located within a specified number of buses to ensure that system impacts will be limited to a local area.

an existing generation resource that intends to divert a material amount of its capacity to serve a new large load at the same location should first submit to a study by the transmission provider to determine whether the diversion of that generation capacity will undermine reliable transmission.

letters.desc: Terraflux supports treating co-located and near-located load-plus-generation pairs as hybrid facilities studied together.
quotes: We agree with the third principle's assertion that both co-located and near-located load plus generation facilities should be studied together as hybrid facilities, rather than forced to be studied as one separate load interconnection request and one separate generation interconnection request. We propose that 'near-located' means within three busbar substations of each other, while 'co-located' means within the same busbar substation.

letters.desc: Tesla strongly endorses studying hybrid facilities on the basis of injection and withdrawal rights to incentivize colocation, and asks that behind-the-meter load and storage count toward the point of interconnection limit and toward offsetting generation loss.
quotes: Tesla strongly endorses the fifth principle, which notes that hybrid facilities should be studied based on the amount of injection and/or withdrawal rights requested to incentivize colocation and efficiency buildout.
We suggest that any additional load or battery energy storage systems (BESS) installed behind-the-meter (BTM) at large load facilities count towards the point of interconnection (POI) limit.

Tesla believes that capacity additions behind the same POI that offset generation “loss” to serve load should be permitted with expedited reviews, assuming the system maintains consistent or similar POI import/export limitations.

letters.desc: Flexible loads can anchor new generation projects and unlock financing in transmission-constrained areas. The filer notes that co-location raises questions about which transmission charges apply at a shared POI.
quotes: In instances where utilities do not have to build more transmission to connect flexible loads, they can increase revenue on the same infrastructure, wires, and substations. Prior to TDSP rate adjustments, this increased revenue can, in turn, help pay for additional transmission projects assuming guidelines have been developed outlining what transmission charges apply to these loads when they are co-located, at the same POI.
Flexible loads can serve as anchor tenants for new generation projects and unlock financing for transmission-constrained generation pockets.

letters.desc: TBA urges a clear policy permitting co-location and adjacent siting of generation and flexible loads as hybrid facilities. Hybrid configurations should be studied on net load, and the generation component should retain the ability to offer capacity into markets when the load can separately curtail.
quotes: TBA strongly encourages the Commission to adopt a clear policy supporting the co-location and adjacent location of generation and flexible loads (forms of dispatchable, curtailable 'hybrid facilities,' as that term is used in the ANOPR).

Designation as a hybrid facility should not prevent the generation component of the facility from offering its capacity into the market where the co-located or adjacent load can separately curtail and does not need the capacity.

letters.desc: Tract supports optional joint study of co-located load and generation but opposes requiring it, arguing that flexibility in hybrid study elections is needed to accommodate diverse commercial arrangements.
quotes: Tract supports DOE's proposal to study load and hybrid facilities together with generating facilities located at the same point of interconnection. Such joint study process should be at the option of both the load and generation customer and should be designed in such a way to result in faster and/or less costly interconnection for both the load and the generator.
